topic: Retinal detachment: presentation and emergency management
scope: Open summary of a CME review of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment as an ophthalmic emergency.

keyRecommendations.text: Typical symptoms are light flashes, floaters, or a dark curtain. Myopia and prior cataract surgery are the main epidemiologic risk factors.
All patients should be seen by an ophthalmologist on the same day symptoms arise.
Treatment is scleral buckle, vitrectomy, or both. Anatomical success is about 85–90%. Vitrectomy is followed by lens opacification in more than 70%.

clinicalBottomLine: Treat flashes, floaters, or a curtain as a same-day ophthalmology emergency; earlier review keeps a better chance that the macula is still attached.
